environment.baselineFailure: Streaming DSV public APIs must exist

prompt:
Implement a production-quality streaming CSV/TSV import API in this real d3-dsv repository, for importing large workspace data files without collecting the complete input in memory. Preserve all existing public methods, synchronous behavior, dependencies, package metadata and original tests.

Add parseRowsStream(source, options?) and parseStream(source, options?) methods to dsvFormat(delimiter). Export csvParseRowsStream, csvParseStream, tsvParseRowsStream and tsvParseStream from src/index.js and the built bundles. Each returns an AsyncIterator/AsyncIterable yielding parsed rows; parseRowsStream yields string arrays, parseStream consumes the first row as column names and yields ordinary objects with safe own properties (including __proto__, constructor and prototype). Missing cells are empty strings, extra cells ignored, repeated column names use the last value as synchronous d3-dsv does. Empty input produces no rows and does not call onColumns. Empty records, trailing delimiters/newlines, quoted delimiters, escaped quotes and embedded newlines follow existing well-formed DSV behavior. Strip a single initial Unicode BOM; preserve BOM elsewhere. Streaming methods accept exactly one UTF-16 code-unit delimiter other than quote, CR or LF; reject unsupported delimiters when the streaming method is consumed, without changing legacy dsvFormat behavior.

source is a synchronous or asynchronous iterable of strings, or an iterable of Uint8Array/Buffer UTF-8 chunks; its mode is selected by the first nonempty chunk, empty chunks are ignored, mixed nonempty string/byte chunks are rejected. Preserve Unicode when every UTF-8 byte boundary or surrogate pair is split. Invalid UTF-8 rejects with code DSV_UTF8; non-string/non-Uint8Array chunks and invalid option/source shapes reject with DSV_INVALID. Browser ReadableStream async iteration and Node Readable async iteration must work. Keep the new core browser-safe with no Node-specific imports, globals, eval or new Function. Existing synchronous implementations may retain their own internals.

options.row is an optional awaited mapper; parseRowsStream calls row(values,index), parseStream calls row(object,index,columns). index is zero-based among parsed logical data records before filtering (the object header is excluded); null or undefined skips a row, other values are yielded unchanged. options.onColumns is supported by parseStream only; await it once with the complete columns before delivering any data row. Do not pull another upstream chunk while awaiting either callback, or while the consumer is paused after a yielded row. Backpressure must bound retention to the current input chunk and incomplete record, not the total stream. Do not eagerly pull from the source before next() is called. The iterator must yield a complete available row before requesting a subsequent upstream chunk, even when the next pull would never resolve. Chunk boundaries can split CRLF, doubled quotes, multibyte UTF-8 and all parser states.

options.signal supports AbortSignal. An already-aborted signal rejects with signal.reason exactly, before acquiring/pulling the source iterator or invoking callbacks. Aborting while source.next(), row() or onColumns() is pending promptly rejects the active next() with the exact reason. Call source.return() once when closing early, on parsing/mapper/source errors, or on cancellation after iterator acquisition; do not call it after normal exhaustion. An uncooperative pending source.next()/return() cannot prevent cancellation from settling. Consume late promise rejection and do not deliver late rows or start more callbacks after cancellation. Consumer break/return also closes the source exactly once. Remove abort listeners after success, failure and cancellation. A source or mapper exception propagates unchanged.

Malformed quoted input is rejected instead of silently accepted: quotes only open at field start, doubled quotes escape quote, and a closing quote must be followed by delimiter, line ending or EOF. Unterminated quotes and stray characters after a closing quote throw DSV_SYNTAX with nonempty message and integer line/column >=1 and rowIndex >=0; line/column refer to physical decoded text (CRLF counts as one line break), rowIndex counts logical records including a header if present. Error detection is incremental and unaffected by chunking. Preserve correctly emitted prior rows; do not emit a malformed row.

Optional maxFieldLength, maxRowLength and maxRows are positive safe integers; omitted limits are unlimited. maxFieldLength counts decoded field UTF-16 units; maxRowLength counts decoded input UTF-16 units in a logical record, including quote/delimiter/quoted-newline characters and excluding the record's terminal CR/LF. maxRows counts logical records after any header and before mapping/filtering. Reject with DSV_LIMIT as soon as a configured limit is exceeded; do not consume the remainder of an unbounded source. Reject unknown options. parseRowsStream rejects onColumns, which belongs to header-based parsing.

Deliver focused maintained tests under test (existing Mocha style), covering every chunk cut for a representative quoted Unicode/CRLF fixture, async mapping, backpressure, headers, BOM, malformed input and exact limit boundaries, early consumer exit, late rejections, source failures and cancellation/listener cleanup. Add docs/streaming.md, update README.md, and runnable offline examples/streaming-import.js using a real temporary CSV file, async iteration, filtering and cleanup. Verify a browser-safe built bundle with CSP-style dynamic code generation disabled, and verify package consumption outside the checkout after packing into an exclusive temporary output directory. Run all original tests, the new tests, lint, bundle build and example; report actual checks and limitations. Continue autonomously until implementation, maintained tests, docs, example and validation are complete. Do not publish or commit.
